recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not restore FHIR-6108's original create-with-id 400 behavior because FHIR-9102 superseded it; the current update-without-id wording already satisfies the remaining applicable seed concern.
issue_request: FHIR-6108 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core-http and asked the RESTful API text to clarify server behavior, HTTP status, response body, and OperationOutcome guidance when create is submitted with an id and update is submitted without the required id.
initial_application: The issue was applied by svn revision 6373, now git commit 3ef34e803fc9ec8688a0d3612f3583d349bf134f, which added HTTP 400 and OperationOutcome wording to the update and create sections of source/http.html.
additional_context: FHIR-9102 was a later Published/Persuasive with Modification decision that changed POST/create id handling so servers SHALL ignore ids supplied on POST; commit 28ccbf99f4e46e92a3f110ad1d06bd715ce95a56 implemented that replacement. FHIR-17906 and FHIR-20390 later clarified conditional update Resource.id handling, but they do not change the direct PUT requirement checked for this seed.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html still says a direct update body SHALL include an id matching the URL id and that a missing or mismatched id gets HTTP 400 with an OperationOutcome recommended. The create section intentionally follows FHIR-9102 by ignoring supplied ids, and the nearby create error text already recommends OperationOutcome bodies for invalid or rejected creates.

related_jiras.note: Later Published decision changed POST/create ids from an error to a SHALL-ignore rule.
Clarified conditional update no-match and one-match behavior after the seed.
Clarified that conditional update bullets refer to Resource.id and preserved 400/OperationOutcome guidance for conflicting Resource.id.
